text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Debt traded sideways at higher levels late as both U.S. Treasury market gains and a sense Germany's economic recovery is still sputtering supported the market. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.89, up 0.18 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts locked in a healthy 24/32 gain on hopes interest rates are not going to rise in either the UK or the U.S. this week. Comments from Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke over the weekend that recent data has justified his decision to leave UK rates on hold made markets hopeful rates would stay on hold after Wednesday's monetary meeting. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-24/32, up 25/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures recovered from session lows after U.S. bonds reacted favourably to a larger than expected decline in a U.S. January purchasing managers survey, while PIBOR contracts continued to come pressure. The March bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.64, up 0.16 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Concern that the goal of first-tier European economic and monetary union (EMU) is once more slipping beyond Italy's reach took a weighty toll on its debt markets. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.30, down 1.28 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened unchanged to slightly lower amid cautiousness and profit-taking preceeding a busy calendar of economic data and a day before a scheduled Federal Reserve policy meeting. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-05/32, up 23/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.74 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese government bond futures ended the session flat. Volume was an extremely thin 23,337 contracts. The March contract rose as high as 126.62 shortly after the open, following Friday's rise in U.S. Treasuries and weekend media reports that Sakura Bank Ltd had rejected a rehabilitation plan proposed by trouble loan firm Apollo Leasing Co. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.32, down 0.23 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity was overshadowed by four emerging sovereign borrowers announcing plans for Eurobond issues -- three in marks and one in dollars. The most immediate will be from Mexico, a 1.0 billion mark 12-year bond planned for launch on Tuesday. Russia's proposed 1.0 billion mark offering will likely be the most interesting after its debut deal last year. Brazil, with a 500 million mark 10-year offering, and Colombia, with a $750 million 10-year due next week, completed the quartet.
